cards.explanation: The reason he gives is that the LORD heard his appeal for mercy. He says, "I love the LORD, for He has heard my voice…" and that voice was his appeal for mercy. He doesn't start with a list of what he got. He starts with the fact that somebody listened when he cried out, friends. I think that's the kind of love that sticks around.

The answer is False. The psalmist says, "Because He has inclined His ear to me, I will call on Him as long as I live." He doesn't retire from prayer once he's been heard. He signs up for life, friends. That's a man who found a good thing and isn't about to stop.

The answer is True, and the order matters. In verse 3 the ropes of death entangled him and the anguish of Sheol overcame him. Then he says, "Then I called on the name of the LORD: “O LORD, deliver my soul!”" First the trouble, then the call, friends.

The answer is gracious and righteous and full of compassion. That's his exact list: "The LORD is gracious and righteous; our God is full of compassion." Notice he says "our God" there, not just "my God." He got the mercy he begged for, and now he describes the LORD with these words, bakers. Gracious, righteous, compassionate. Hard to improve on that.

The answer is the simplehearted. The psalmist says, "The LORD preserves the simplehearted; I was helpless, and He saved me." Look how he puts those two things side by side, friends. He was helpless, and He saved me. That line makes me want to stand up in my apron and cheer.

The reason is that the LORD has been good to his soul. He says, "Return to your rest, O my soul, for the LORD has been good to you." His reason for rest is what the LORD has already done for him, friends. I think it's a little like telling yourself to unclench after the oven timer finally goes off.

The two blanks are tears and stumbling. The psalmist says, "For You have delivered my soul from death, my eyes from tears, my feet from stumbling." He's talking straight to the LORD now, saying "You." That's his whole list, friends: soul, eyes and feet. And I'm a stamper who's been dropped on a kitchen floor, so I know how much that last one matters.

The answer is True. He says, "I will walk before the LORD in the land of the living." He was staring at death a few verses back (Psalm 116:3), and now he's making plans to keep walking, friends. I think that's a man who knows what a gift his next step is.

The answer is in his alarm. The psalmist says, "In my alarm I said, “All men are liars!”" He tells us he said it when he was alarmed, and he doesn't hide it, friends. I think that's honest of him. I've said some silly things when I was alarmed myself, mostly to a cookie tin.

The answer is the cup of salvation. The psalmist says, "I will lift the cup of salvation and call on the name of the LORD." His answer to "How can I repay…" isn't a purchase, friends. He lifts a cup and calls on the LORD's name. I'm relieved, because my budget is a quarter and a mustache.

The answer is False. The psalmist says, "I will fulfill my vows to the LORD in the presence of all His people." Nothing quiet or hidden about that, friends. He plans to do it in the presence of the LORD's people.

The answer is that their death is valuable to Him. "Precious in the sight of the LORD is the death of His saints." That's what "precious" is telling us, friends: their death matters to Him, it's valuable in His sight. The psalm doesn't say more about it than that, so I'll let that line stand.

The answer is True. Verse 16 says, "Truly, O LORD, I am Your servant; I am Your servant, the son of Your maidservant; You have broken my bonds." He says "Your servant" twice, and then the bonds line lands. Notice who does the breaking, friends: "You."

The answer is thanksgiving. The psalmist says, "I will offer to You a sacrifice of thanksgiving and call on the name of the LORD." He asked how to repay, and here's what he offers, friends. It's a sacrifice of thanksgiving, with calling on the LORD's name right alongside it.

The answer is Jerusalem. The psalmist says, "…in the courts of the LORD’s house, in your midst, O Jerusalem. Hallelujah!" He talks to the city itself, friends, like he's inviting it to listen. He wants his vows kept right where everyone can see.
